translation.title: Prednisolone Valeroacetate Lotion
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for eczema, the dermatitis group (including progressive keratoderma of the fingers and chronic lichen simplex), the prurigo group (itchy eruptions, including papular urticaria), insect bites, psoriasis, and pustulosis of the palms and soles.
translation.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area several times a day, adjusting suitably according to the symptoms.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, or if you have a skin infection (tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, ringworm, shingles, herpes simplex, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies or pubic lice), eczematous otitis externa with a perforated eardrum, ulcers (except Behcet's disease), burns or frostbite of second-degree deep severity or worse, perioral dermatitis, common acne, or rosacea. Before using it, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if you are breastfeeding, or for infants, small children and the elderly. Do not use it in the eyes. Do not use it for purposes other than treatment, such as after makeup or shaving. Do not use an occlusive dressing without a doctor's supervision. Stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist if adverse reactions occur, such as infectious impetigo, folliculitis, candidiasis, ringworm, boils, skin irritation, stinging pain, fever, a burning sensation, a rash, redness, flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, heat rash, worsening of wounds, pressure sores, or pustulosis. When used on the eyelid skin, increased eye pressure and glaucoma may occur, and systemic absorption of topical corticosteroids may cause reversible Cushing's syndrome, high blood sugar, or diabetes.
